title: A surviving contraction step removes one vertex
statement: Let $s$ and $t$ be states of the contraction process, each a multigraph together with a distinguished cut, and suppose that $t$ arises from $s$ by a surviving step, that is, $t$ is obtained by contracting some edge $e$ of the multigraph of $s$ that does not cross the distinguished cut of $s$. Then the number of vertices of the multigraph of $t$ equals the number of vertices of the multigraph of $s$ minus $1$ (with the difference taken in $\bbn$).
hypotheses_covered: t arises from s by a surviving step (contraction along a non-crossing edge of s's multigraph)
replaced:
If $t$ is obtained from $s$ by a surviving step, then $t.G$ has exactly one vertex fewer
than $s.G$.
